description: Asset manifest for the kid-facing game layer. Resolved by experiments/game_layer.py. Paths are relative to assets/game/.

mascot_variants._doc: Pip is a rounded fox-raccoon hybrid -- deliberately not a real species, so children do not import real-animal associations into the similarity judgment. There is exactly ONE variant, by design; see _single_variant_doc.
mascot_variants._single_variant_doc: The gendered boy/girl variants were REMOVED. Selecting the mascot from the participant's gender put a systematically different image on screen for every trial, which is a presentation confound with any across-gender comparison -- and one that would have forced every downstream analysis to stratify by variant forever. One character for everyone removes it at the source. The structure appears here so a future variant (a translation, a high-contrast set) can be added without a schema change; participant_data.mascot_variant is still recorded so a session can always be audited.

rooms._doc: Room framing per stimulus condition. One room = one block = one break point. Names are deliberately ABSTRACT (place words, not category words): a room called 'the toy room' over a triplet containing toys would hint at the grouping we are trying to measure. Keyed by the condition code used in experiments/two_tier_experiment.py.
rooms._backdrop_doc: Backdrops advance ONE PER ROOM, not per condition: c1 is a bare shell and each step is a little more furnished, so the castle visibly fills up as the session goes on. Rooms beyond the sequence re-use the later, fullest ones.
rooms._progression_doc: One entry per MANSION room, in room-index order (backdrop_for_room walks this by index). Nine entries for the nine rooms, so in a normal session every room takes its own and the repeat fallback never fires. Indices 2 and 5 are the game rooms (castle_state.ARCADE_ROOMS) and carry art made for their game -- a night sky for Star Catcher, pale tilework for Bubble Pop -- which is what the arcade screen paints behind the game and what its grid tile shows. repeat_from is 7 so that a build with MORE rooms than art draws from indices 6-8, the three plain decoration rooms: the two arcade backdrops must never be handed to a decoration room, and they are the last thing the tail should offer. The rest of collection/ (c1, c3-c8, c11) is unused on disk rather than deleted; drop any of it back in here to change a room.
rooms._shared_doc: All three conditions currently share this progression. Echo and theatre keep their own single-image entries below for when their art exists; set `progression` inside a condition to override.

sounds._variety_doc: A value may be a single path (unchanged) or a LIST of paths, in which case GameLayer.play() picks one at random per call via its own rng and caches per resolved file rather than per key -- see game_layer.py. `sticker` uses this for placement-sound variety; `sticker_2`/`sticker_3` are optional and the list just has one entry until they exist.

music._doc: Background music under the opening/closing cutscenes, the playground, and the shop. Cutscene tracks start the moment the cutscene begins -- panel art or the text-only fallback alike -- and stop the moment it ends, so they can never land over a trial or a Tier 2 stimulus clip. Same track for both open/close by default; give `close` its own file to differ. `playground` and `shop` LOOP for as long as their screen is open (untimed, see GameLayer.play_music's `loop` param) and stop the moment the child leaves for a different 'place' -- see _show_playground_screen/_leave_playground/_enter_shop/_leave_shop in two_tier_experiment.py. See GameLayer.play_music/stop_music (experiments/game_layer.py) and js/src/music.js.
music._fade_doc: Every track fades rather than cuts -- starting under speech and panel art, a track snapping straight to full volume (or straight to silence mid-scene) reads as a glitch. Capped by reduced-stimulation mode like the cutscene's own visual cross-fade.

theme._palette_doc: Pip's palette: muted-but-warm soft teal / sandy yellow / dusty rose. Inviting without the high-saturation overstimulation of a typical children's game. These three are the CHARACTER and SCENERY colours; see the selection note below for why they do not extend to the highlight.
theme._selection_color_doc: Deliberately NOT green and NOT red -- those read as correct/incorrect to a child and would imply the free choice was graded. Note this is why the highlight stays blue rather than adopting the palette above: soft teal reads as greenish and dusty rose as reddish, so neither is safe for the one element that marks the child's own choice.
theme._progress_fill_doc: Sandy yellow, not the previous green. A progress bar is not response feedback, but a green fill that advances after each choice is an avoidable success cue.
theme._font_doc: Bundled UI font. Rodin Bokutoh is the rounded/soft cut, which suits a children's game better than the straight-sided NewRodin; both are listed so either can be selected by changing `family`. Set `family` to null or remove the block to fall back to the system font. NOTE for maintainers: these files are loaded by READING THE BYTES, because QFontDatabase.addApplicationFont(path) returns -1 for them on macOS even though the files are valid OpenType. See _load_fonts in experiments/game_layer.py.

accessibility._doc: Defaults for reduced-stimulation mode (config key: Gamify_Reduced_Motion). Applied when working with children who are sensitive to movement/sound, including autistic participants.

cutscene._doc: Story panels shown at the start and end of a session. Each panel pairs a wide image with one dialogue line, drawn in a box along the bottom; panels cross-fade. Missing images degrade to the text-only cutscene, so the session still runs while art is being made.
cutscene._composition_doc: Panels must keep their bottom ~20% visually calm -- the dialogue box covers it. See docs/ASSET_BRIEF.md §4.
cutscene._panels_doc: 1 = Pip waves, castle behind him. 2 = cutaway castle, every room empty, Pip looking up at them. 3 = the same castle decorated, Pip looking at it. Panel 2 carries two lines because the premise and the invitation are separate beats; the image holds while the text changes.

cursors._doc: Optional custom cursor art for the playground. Omit a key and Qt's open-hand / closed-hand cursors are used, which already read as "you can pick this up" and "you are holding it" on every platform. A named-but-missing file falls back the same way rather than leaving a blank cursor with nothing to aim.
cursors._hotspot_doc: hotspot is [x, y] in pixels within the SCALED image (size_px), i.e. the exact point that counts as the pointer tip. Per-kind overrides: point_hotspot / drag_hotspot.

castle._doc: Playground placement (Stage 9). Stickers go ANYWHERE the child puts them -- there are no slots and no snapping, and overlapping is allowed. Deciding where is the only real autonomy the game layer offers, and a snap target quietly makes that decision instead of the child.
castle._coords_doc: Positions are recorded RELATIVE to the room canvas (0..1) in game_state.castle.placements, so a castle laid out on one screen renders identically on another and survives a window resize. Drops are clamped to keep the sticker fully on screen and clear of the pending-sticker tray; see EDGE_MARGIN_REL in experiments/playground.py.

stickers._doc: 2-4 stickers are awarded per completed ROOM. The count for every room is drawn ONCE at session start, before the first response exists -- see experiments/castle_state.py. Purely cosmetic and never contingent on WHAT was picked, only on finishing the room.
stickers._codepoint_doc: Every sticker MUST be an astral emoji (U+1F300 and above). Emoji in the BMP symbol blocks (⭐ U+2B50, ⛵ U+26F5, ☀ U+2600, ☁ U+2601) also have a monochrome TEXT glyph, and Qt reaches a system symbol font before the colour emoji font, so they render as thin line art next to full-colour stickers. Appending U+FE0F does NOT fix it -- ☀️ and ☁️ carried the variation selector and still came out monochrome, because Qt font matching on macOS ignores it. Astral codepoints have no monochrome glyph to fall back to, which is why the rule is about the codepoint and not the variation selector. tests/test_game_layer.py::test_stickers_render_in_colour_not_line_art enforces it.
stickers._art_doc: Deliberately generic castle-decoration subjects, NOT objects from the stimulus set. Sticker art that matched a room's stimulus category would turn the reward into a hint about the grouping the trial is measuring. This is the open question flagged in docs/GAMIFICATION_ROADMAP.md §7, resolved here in favour of decoration.

furniture._doc: Purchased, not earned -- unlike stickers, furniture is bought in the shop with coins the child already earned by finishing rooms. Placed the same way stickers are (drag/tap into a room), just larger. Same stimulus-neutrality rule as stickers applies: see tests/test_game_layer.py::test_no_sticker_is_a_stimulus_object, extended to this pool.
furniture._placeholder_doc: Missing PNGs degrade to the emoji, same as stickers. Furniture-specific naming rule: no `id`/`label` may be a literal named furniture word (chair/table/lamp/couch/sofa are stimulus-set words).
furniture._variant_doc: Each collectible has 4 palette VARIANTS (see docs/ASSET_BRIEF.md's furniture theme prompts) -- `pool` is variant-level, one entry per `{base}_{theme}` image. `base` groups an entry's variants for ShopState.buy_furniture, which draws a random not-yet-owned variant per purchase; a catalog entry shows 'Sold out' once all 4 are owned. `bases` carries the generic (theme-independent) label/emoji shown before any variant is drawn. See GameLayer.furniture_variants/furniture_base_by_id.

backgrounds._doc: Alternate room backdrops the child can unlock and equip from the shop, distinct from the fixed per-condition progression in rooms.progression (which every child sees regardless of the shop). Equipping one overrides that room's backdrop for the rest of the session -- see ShopState.background_overrides / equip_background.

animals._doc: Companion critters for the mansion. NOT bought or placed directly: the child buys an invitation letter (shop.catalog buy_invitation) and one of these arrives by itself in a random unlocked room, moving to another room after each block (see CastleState.invite_guest / move_guests). A guest is scenery the child receives, not an item they arrange -- which is why it has no placement of its own to drag. Deliberately fantastical, not real species: Pip is the game's one fixed mascot by design (see mascot._doc), and a real-animal name/likeness here would risk the same thing that rule guards against -- importing a real-world category the child could map onto a trial's similarity judgment. Same stimulus-neutrality rule as stickers/furniture: no id or label may double as a stimulus-set word.

shop._doc: Catalog and pricing, kept separate from the furniture/backgrounds art pools above so prices can be tuned without touching art data. Coins come from CastleState.coins_awarded (earned, response-blind, same schedule as stickers) -- the shop only ever spends what was already earned that way. See experiments/shop_state.py / js/src/shop.js.
shop._pricing_doc: Placeholder prices for a coin economy that averages MIN_COINS_PER_TRIAL..MAX_COINS_PER_TRIAL per TRIAL, weighted toward the low end (experiments/castle_state.py COIN_WEIGHTS), not per room -- a room's total now scales with its trial count instead of being a flat draw. That earns roughly 3x what the old flat per-room draw did over a typical room, so every price below is the prior placeholder x3. Tuning these against actual session length/room count is still a product decision, not an engineering one.

catalog.label: Invitation letter
catalog._doc: Animals are no longer bought and placed. The child buys an INVITATION and one of the animals (manifest.animals.pool, drawn with the shop's own purchase rng) turns up by itself in a random unlocked room -- then moves to a different room after each block completes. Priced near the middle of the four direct animal buys it replaces (20, 16, 34, 26) since it still buys exactly one animal, just not a chosen one. See CastleState.invite_guest / move_guests.

urn, chandelier, aurora and mossling are exclusive to this box -- not sold directly -- so the box has something worth opening for. urn/chandelier are listed per VARIANT (see furniture._variant_doc) since the box draws one exact item, not a base id to re-roll through buy_furniture's own variant draw.
